themes_detail.label: Vendor enforcement surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints spiked to 6 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 1.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 380% increase (z-score: 4.91)—suggesting either a new enforcement push, concentrated vendor activity, or emerging quality/safety issues in street vending across Morningside Heights.
evidence: 6 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs 1.2 weekly baseline (8-week average)
No recent news mentions or community board discussion of vendor issues on record
reporting_angles: Contact DSNY/DOH to learn if a new enforcement initiative or sting operation launched this week; interview vendors about sudden increased scrutiny
Canvass Amsterdam Avenue and 125th Street corridor for vendor complaints; ask whether quality, sanitation, or permit issues prompted the spike

themes_detail.label: Park rule violations spike
themes_detail.summary: Park rule violation complaints exploded to 4 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 0.1 per week—a 3,100% spike (z-score: 11.72, the single highest anomaly in the dataset)—pointing to either a specific incident, new congregations, or enforcement focus in Morningside Park or nearby green spaces.
evidence: 4 park rule violation complaints last week vs 0.1 weekly baseline (8-week average)
3,100% spike; highest z-score (11.72) across all detected anomalies
Morningside Park is primary green space in district; no prior news coverage of violations
reporting_angles: Visit Morningside Park; observe conditions and speak to Parks Department about what triggered complaints (unauthorized gatherings, after-hours use, sanitation issues)
Interview Columbia University Community Safety and Parks enforcement; determine if new policy or incident prompted 4-complaint cluster

themes_detail.label: Water quality complaints rise
themes_detail.summary: Water quality complaints jumped to 3 LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 0.4 per week—a 700% increase (z-score: 5.42)—raising questions about tap water safety, discoloration, or taste/odor across the district during a week when broader water infrastructure concerns may be emerging.
evidence: 3 water quality complaints last week vs 0.4 weekly baseline (8-week average)
Concurrent with 3,430 heat/hot water complaints over 90 days (possibly related to aging water infrastructure)
reporting_angles: Contact DEP to ask if there was a water main break, hydrant flushing, or quality issue in Morningside Heights last week; check water quality test results
Contact Columbia University and key institutions (hospitals, schools) to determine if they received multiple water complaints simultaneously

themes_detail.label: Homeless assistance calls spike
themes_detail.summary: Homeless person assistance complaints rose to 12 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 2.9 per week—a 317% increase (z-score: 3.2)—indicating either worsening homelessness, new encampments, or heightened public concern in Morningside Heights and Hamilton Heights.
evidence: 12 homeless person assistance complaints last week vs 2.9 weekly baseline (8-week average)
Recurring community board budget request for outreach services to homeless and homebound populations (indicating long-standing underlying issue)
reporting_angles: Map the 12 complaints geographically; identify if clustering in one area (e.g., subway stations, parks) or district-wide; speak to residents about visibility and safety concerns
Interview local social services providers and NYPD about whether new encampments emerged or crisis escalated last week; tie to budget request for outreach funding

themes_detail.label: Animal abuse reports jump
themes_detail.summary: Animal abuse complaints spiked to 8 TWO WEEKS AGO from a baseline of 2.8 per week—a 191% increase (z-score: 4.82)—suggesting either a specific incident, neighborhood awareness campaign, or pattern of animal neglect in Morningside Heights.
evidence: 8 animal abuse complaints 2 weeks ago vs 2.8 weekly baseline (8-week average)
No subsequent complaints detected at same level; suggests either isolated incident or one-time reporting surge
reporting_angles: Contact ASPCA and NYPD Animal Cruelty Investigations to identify the 8 complaints and determine if they involved one location/perpetrator or multiple unrelated incidents
If a single incident, profile the case and animal welfare outcome; if multiple, explore whether new awareness or enforcement activity triggered reports
